conceptual assets.information: The first operand word processed by the bit-manipulation operations; the operation results depend on this value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The operand can be exposed through the computed result and data-dependent completion behavior at res_o and valid_o (274-285, 492-502). The operand can be changed when rs1_i is captured and thereby cause an incorrect result (187-189, 389-456).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe res_o or alter the captured first operand so a bit-manipulation result reveals or incorrectly processes that data.

conceptual assets.information: The second operand word used by binary bit-manipulation operations such as logical operations, shift-add, packing and carry-less multiplication.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The second operand contributes to the value returned through res_o, which can expose information derived from it (389-456, 492-496). Changing rs2_i changes the captured operand and can produce an incorrect result (187-190, 389-456).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the returned result or modify rs2_i before capture to disclose or corrupt the second operand's operation.

conceptual assets.information: The shift amount or bit-position operand used to select shift stages and individual bit operations.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing shamt_i changes the captured shift amount and the selected bit or shift result, producing an incorrect output (187, 191, 298, 343, 429-433).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter shamt_i so the operation shifts by a different amount or modifies a different bit.

conceptual assets.information: The comparison decision selecting which source operand is returned by the maximum operation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the comparison decision captured in less_reg changes the operand selected by the maximum operation and can therefore produce an incorrect result (188, 402).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could modify the comparison indication so the maximum operation returns the wrong operand.

conceptual assets.information: The control decision that identifies and accepts a bit-manipulation operation for execution; the coprocessor depends on it to capture operands and start or complete an operation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the coprocessor-enable and command-valid decision can prevent operand capture or cause the wrong operation to be accepted (164, 187-207). The same decision can block operation start and prevent a valid result from being produced (199-220).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the acceptance control inactive or corrupt command validation so operations are rejected, mis-dispatched or never produce a result.

conceptual assets.information: The controller state, multi-cycle counters and completion state that sequence iterative shifts or carry-less multiplication and release a valid result. No whole-value input port carries this internal state; it is generated from accepted commands and clocked progress.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Modifying the controller state, iteration counters or completion flag can skip, repeat or terminate steps and make the returned result invalid (172, 202-220, 236-257, 355-362). Holding the state or valid flag in a busy or inactive condition can block completion and withhold valid_o (218-220, 491-502).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the progress state or counter to an unintended value, causing an incorrect result or preventing valid_o from signalling completion.

conceptual assets.information: The computed result of the selected bit-manipulation operation, returned to the processor for write-back or further execution.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The computed result is directly exposed at res_o, which can reveal information derived from the operands (389-480, 492-496). The result can be altered by corrupting operands, command selection, comparison control or computation state (389-456, 461-496). The valid-controlled output register can withhold the result even after an operation is accepted (485-497).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe res_o, corrupt an input or internal computation, or suppress valid so that the result is disclosed, incorrect or withheld.

considered, not kept.reason: The opcode and funct fields only select the operation or result form, so the Operation selectors rule makes them part of the operation rather than a separate conceptual asset (132-161, 461-480).
The cpu_trap field only refines the controller's abort and completion decision, so the Processor context fields rule bars it as an independent piece (218-220).
The EN_FAST_SHIFT and EN_ZBA/EN_ZBB/EN_ZBKC/EN_ZBKB/EN_ZBS values only select logic at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time (28-33, 230-231, 294-295, 349-350, 378-379).
